purpose: Reproduce and independently challenge direct-wave/horizon associations using public numerical-relativity strain.
status: pre-registered benchmark specification; no results claimed

primary_counteranalysis.title: The Direct Wave is Not a Meaningful Test of Horizon Properties
primary_counteranalysis.scope: equal-mass, quasicircular, non-precessing SXS systems with remnant |chi_f| >= about 0.5
claims_to_test: direct-wave instantaneous frequency does not generally track 2*Omega_H
direct-wave damping does not generally track surface gravity kappa and evolves over short fitting intervals
the apparent frequency coincidence near chi_f about 0.69 is not a universal horizon relation
mapping direct-wave fit parameters to horizon observables can yield spurious apparent area-law violations

published_filter_configuration.reason: remove spherical-spheroidal mode mixing in SXS data

analysis_dimensions: four predeclared fitting intervals around merger; exact bounds must be transcribed from the paper supplement before execution
QNM filter basis and removed-mode set
waveform extraction radius and extrapolation order
mass ratio and spin configuration where an expanded SXS corpus is used
required_observables: instantaneous direct-wave real frequency divided by 2*Omega_H
instantaneous damping rate -Im(omega) divided by kappa
frequency and damping evolution over fitting interval
NR remnant horizon area from final mass and spin
horizon area inferred from direct-wave-derived Omega_H and kappa
negative_controls: held-out SXS simulations not used for fitting
acceptance: reproduce the published counteranalysis figures under pinned input and filter versions
reproduce the GW250114 direct-wave paper result under its declared assumptions
distinguish extraction reproducibility from horizon interpretation
report calibration, false-positive rate, and held-out predictive performance
independent implementation reproduces the same quantitative conclusions
claim_ceiling: A filtered component may be reproducible without being a measurement of horizon frequency or surface gravity. A direct-wave-derived area estimate is not a Hawking-area-law test unless the mapping to horizon observables is independently validated over parameter space.
